statements.gas-pressure: Pressure is the force exerted per unit area, P = F/A. A gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container because its molecules collide with those walls, so a small force on a small area can give a larger pressure than a large force spread over a large one.
statements.mean-free-path: The mean free path is the average distance a molecule travels between collisions. Gas molecules travel at hundreds of meters per second but collide billions of times a second, so the mean free path is short, and it grows as the pressure falls.
statements.standard-temperature-and-pressure: Standard conditions of temperature and pressure, STP, are 273.15 K (0 °C) and 1 atm (101.325 kPa), the conditions chemists agree to report the volume of a gas against. At STP one mole of any ideal gas occupies about 22.4 L.
statements.mole-fraction-and-partial-pressure: The partial pressure of a gas in a mixture is its mole fraction times the total pressure. The relation lets us move between the composition of a mixture and the pressures of its components without computing each pressure from the ideal gas law.

new.name: Force, $F$
new.statement: A force is a push or a pull on an object. A gas pushes on the walls of its container with a force that comes from the collisions of its molecules with those walls.

new.name: Area, $A$
new.statement: The area of a surface is its extent, measured in square units such as square meters. A force spread over a larger area gives a smaller pressure.

new.name: Acceleration due to gravity, $g$
new.statement: The acceleration due to gravity is the rate at which the speed of a falling object increases near the surface of the earth, about 9.8 m/s². It turns the mass of a column of fluid into the weight that presses on what lies beneath it.

new.name: Pascal (Pa)
new.statement: The pascal is the SI unit of pressure, a force of one newton on an area of one square meter: 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

new.name: Bar
new.statement: The bar is a unit of pressure equal to 100,000 Pa, close to the pressure of the atmosphere at sea level.

new.name: Atmosphere (atm)
new.statement: The standard atmosphere is a unit of pressure equal to 101,325 Pa, the average pressure of the atmosphere at sea level.

new.name: Torr
new.statement: The torr is a unit of pressure equal to 1/760 atm, almost exactly the pressure that supports a column of mercury 1 millimeter high.

new.name: Pounds per square inch (psi)
new.statement: Pounds per square inch is a unit of pressure common in the United States; 1 atm is 14.7 psi.

new.name: Barometer
new.statement: A barometer is a device used to measure atmospheric pressure, usually by the height of the column of liquid the atmosphere supports in an inverted tube.

new.name: Manometer
new.statement: A manometer is a device used to measure the pressure of a gas trapped in a container: a U-shaped tube of liquid whose difference in levels gives the pressure.

new.name: The ideal gas constant, $R$
new.statement: The ideal gas constant R is the constant of proportionality in the ideal gas law, the same for every gas. Its value depends on the units of pressure and volume: 0.08206 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ or 8.314 L kPa mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.

new.name: Molar volume, $V_m$
new.statement: The molar volume of a gas is the volume occupied by 1 mole of it at a given temperature and pressure.

new.name: Standard molar volume
new.statement: The standard molar volume is the volume of 1 mole of gas at STP, about 22.4 L for any gas behaving ideally.

new.name: Partial pressure, $P_A$
new.statement: The partial pressure of a gas in a mixture is the pressure that gas exerts, the pressure it would exert if it alone occupied the container.

new.name: Mole fraction, $X_A = n_A/n_{Total}$
new.statement: The mole fraction of a component of a mixture is its amount in moles divided by the total amount of all the components, a concentration unit that carries no units of its own.

new.name: Vapor pressure of water
new.statement: The vapor pressure of water is the pressure exerted by water vapor in equilibrium with liquid water in a closed container at a specific temperature. It rises with the temperature.

new.name: Diffusion
new.statement: Diffusion is the movement of atoms or molecules from a region of relatively high concentration to one of relatively low concentration, caused by their random motion.

new.name: Effusion
new.statement: Effusion is the escape of gaseous atoms or molecules from a container into a vacuum through very small openings.

new.name: Rate of diffusion
new.statement: The rate of diffusion is the amount of gas passing through a given area in a unit of time.

new.name: Speed, $u$
new.statement: The speed of a particle is the distance it travels divided by the time it takes. The molecules of a gas move at a wide range of speeds.
